w:r.w:t: for BVLOS flights to monitor bison. Complete a high-level SORA assessment by working through all 10 steps.
Aim for the largest useful Flight Geography you can justify while keeping the operation and resulting SAIL proportionate. Keep answers short and explain your reasoning.
Step 1: Proposed Operation / Concept of Operations (ConOps)
What is the operation trying to achieve?
Where will you operate? Define the intended Flight Geography.
What is the maximum operating height?

Define the volumes before doing the risk calculations. The Operational Volume is the Flight Geography + Contingency Volume. The Ground Risk Class footprint is the Operational Volume + Ground Risk Buffer.
Show the Flight Geography, Contingency Volume, Ground Risk Buffer and Adjacent Area. Add the main height limit as a note.
Sketch or paste your map here
What is the highest population density within the iGRC footprint?
What is the maximum speed of the UAS?
What is the maximum characteristic dimension of the UAS?

Use SORA Table 2. For a fixed-wing UAS, the characteristic dimension is the wingspan. Use the designer-defined maximum possible commanded airspeed, not just your planned cruise speed. If the footprint crosses areas with different population densities, use the highest relevant density.
Which ground-risk mitigations are genuinely applicable? Add a short justification or supporting evidence.
Reduced effects of UA impact dynamics
For this exercise, you can state your assumed robustness rather than working through Annex B in detail. Apply any claimed credits in the sequence given in SORA Table 5.
What is the final GRC after the applicable mitigations?
Which initial ARC applies to the Operational Volume, and why?
Are there any relevant NOTAMs, temporary restrictions or special airspace constraints?

Use dronezoner.dk as your starting point and follow the SORA Figure 6 logic. Check the maximum height, controlled/uncontrolled airspace, airport/heliport environment, urban/rural environment and whether the airspace is atypical. Assess the full Operational Volume, not only the nominal route.
Step 5: Strategic Mitigations and Residual ARC
Which strategic mitigation(s) could reduce the air encounter rate?
What is the residual ARC after those mitigations?

Think about changes made before flight, such as time of operation, geographic or altitude restrictions, or airspace structure/coordination. Only reduce the ARC if you can justify that the local encounter rate is lower than the initial classification.
What TMPR level and robustness follow from your residual ARC?
In one or two sentences, what would you use to detect and respond to manned traffic during the BVLOS flight?

Keep this at concept level. Describe the detection/information source and the avoidance response. SORA discusses options such as DAA, cooperative traffic information and operational procedures; the required performance depends on the residual ARC.
Step 7: Specific Assurance and Integrity Level (SAIL)
Use SORA Table 7: the SAIL is derived from the final GRC and residual ARC. Do not choose a SAIL first and work backwards.
What is the lateral size of the Adjacent Area?
What population / assembly-of-people limits are relevant in the Adjacent Area?

For a UA above 250 g, SORA 2.5 sets the Adjacent Area outer limit using the distance flown in 3 minutes at maximum speed, with a minimum of 5 km and maximum of 35 km. Also check the average population density in the Adjacent Area and outdoor assemblies within 1 km of the Operational Volume. The 1 km distance is an assembly-of-people check, not the size of the Adjacent Area.

Use SORA Table 14 to enter the required level (NR / L / M / H). For each OSO that is required, give one short example of how you would implement it or what evidence you would keep. A few words are enough.
Safety-essential components designed to an ADS
System safety and reliability considered in the design
C3 link characteristics appropriate for the operation
Conformity check of the UAS configuration
Operational procedures defined, validated and followed
External services adequate for the operation
Automatic flight-envelope protection from human error
Environmental limits defined, measurable and followed
UAS qualified for adverse environmental conditions
In 4-6 bullets, what would you include in the final CSP?

Think of the CSP as the final safety case: operation description -> safety claims and mitigations -> derived requirements -> compliance evidence -> clear traceability between them. You do not need to build the full portfolio for this exercise.
